title: Git push rejected - Updates were rejected because the remote contains work that you do not have locally
description: I am trying to submit Task 2 by pushing to my branch feature/task-2-frontend, but git keeps rejecting my push with error 'failed to push some refs'.
error_log:
error: failed to push some refs to 'https://github.com/internship/cohort-repo.git'
hint: Updates were rejected because the remote contains work that you do not have locally.
hint: This is usually caused by another repository pushing to the same ref.
hint: See the 'Note about fast-forwards' in 'git push --help' for details.
root_cause: The remote branch had commits that were not present on the local machine (likely from an online README edit or mentor commit), preventing a fast-forward push.
solution_steps:
1. Pull remote changes with rebase:
   `git pull --rebase origin feature/task-2-frontend`
2. If any merge conflicts appear, resolve the conflict markers in your editor and run `git rebase --continue`.
3. Re-push cleanly:
   `git push origin feature/task-2-frontend`
*Tip: Never use `git push --force` on shared branches!*
verified_resolution: Ran git pull --rebase origin branch-name, resolved 1 README conflict, push succeeded immediately.

title: FastAPI ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fastapi' or 'uvicorn'
description: Whenever I try to run `uvicorn main:app --reload` inside VSCode, Python crashes with ModuleNotFoundError even though I ran pip install fastapi.
error_log:
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "backend/main.py", line 1, in <module>
    from fastapi import FastAPI
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fastapi'
root_cause: The Python virtual environment was not activated, causing the command to run against global system Python where dependencies were not installed, or VSCode selected the wrong Python interpreter.
solution_steps:
1. Activate your virtual environment in terminal:
   - Windows PowerShell: `.\venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1`
   - macOS/Linux: `source venv/bin/activate`
2. If venv does not exist, create and install:
   `python -m venv venv`
   `pip install -r requirements.txt`
3. In VS Code: Press `Ctrl+Shift+P` -> Type `Python: Select Interpreter` -> Pick `./venv/Scripts/python.exe`.
verified_resolution: Activated virtual environment in VSCode integrated terminal and re-ran uvicorn successfully.

title: CORS policy blocked: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header present on requested resource
description: My React frontend running at localhost:5173 cannot make API calls to FastAPI backend on localhost:8000 due to CORS error.
error_log: Access to fetch at 'http://localhost:8000/api/chat' from origin 'http://localhost:5173' has been blocked by CORS policy: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is present on the requested resource.
root_cause: FastAPI by default blocks cross-origin requests from frontend dev servers unless CORSMiddleware is explicitly configured.
solution_steps:
1. Import and add `CORSMiddleware` to `main.py`:
```python
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware

app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=["http://localhost:5173", "http://localhost:3000", "*"],
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
)
```
2. Restart the FastAPI server.
verified_resolution: Added CORSMiddleware with allowed origins; React fetch requests resolved with 200 OK.

title: Docker container fails with 'Error response from daemon: Ports are not available: listen tcp 0.0.0.0:8000: bind: address already in use'
description: When running docker compose up or docker run -p 8000:8000, docker crashes claiming port 8000 is already occupied.
error_log: docker: Error response from daemon: Ports are not available: exposing port TCP 0.0.0.0:8000 -> 0.0.0.0:0: listen tcp 0.0.0.0:8000: bind: address already in use.
root_cause: Another process (e.g. background uvicorn or previous orphaned docker container) was already listening on port 8000.
solution_steps:
1. Find the PID using port 8000:
   - Windows: `netstat -ano | findstr :8000`
   - macOS/Linux: `lsof -i :8000`
2. Terminate the blocking process:
   - Windows: `taskkill /PID <PID_NUMBER> /F`
   - macOS/Linux: `kill -9 <PID_NUMBER>`
3. Alternatively, map to another host port:
   `docker run -p 8080:8000 my-image`
verified_resolution: Killed dangling background python process on PID 14220; container started cleanly.

title: OpenAI / HuggingFace API returns 429 Too Many Requests: Rate limit exceeded
description: During query embedding batch execution, the API throws HTTP 429 Too Many Requests and all chatbot responses fail.
error_log: openai.error.RateLimitError: Rate limit reached for default-text-embedding-3-small in organization org-xxx on requests per min (RPM). Status 429.
root_cause: The script was sending parallel synchronous requests in a tight loop without caching or exponential backoff rate limiting.
verified_resolution: Switched to local sentence embeddings with fallback caching; 429 errors eliminated.

title: Git Merge Conflict in main during Pull Request merge
description: My PR on GitHub shows 'This branch has conflicts that must be resolved'. I am terrified of overwriting teammate changes.
error_log:
Auto-merging backend/routes/tasks.py
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in backend/routes/tasks.py
Automatic merge failed; fix conflicts and then commit the result.
root_cause: Both branches modified the same lines in `backend/routes/tasks.py`.
solution_steps:
1. Checkout your feature branch locally:
   `git checkout feature/task-3-routes`
2. Fetch and merge latest main:
   `git fetch origin`
   `git merge origin/main`
3. Open conflicted files in VS Code. Review `<<<<<<< HEAD` (your changes) and `>>>>>>> origin/main` (upstream changes).
4. Select 'Accept Current', 'Accept Incoming', or 'Accept Both Changes' in VS Code Merge Editor.
5. Save file, stage, commit, and push:
   `git add .`
   `git commit -m "fix(merge): resolve conflict with main in tasks.py"`
   `git push origin feature/task-3-routes`
verified_resolution: Guided intern through VS Code merge editor; resolved conflict and PR checks went green.

title: Pytest fails with Database table does not exist during CI automated test run
description: All unit tests pass locally on SQLite, but fail in GitHub Actions CI with sqlite3.OperationalError: no such table: users.
error_log:
sqlite3.OperationalError: no such table: users
FAILED tests/test_auth.py::test_user_registration - sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError: (sqlite3.OperationalError) no such table: users
root_cause: The test runner was not creating database tables prior to executing test fixtures in an ephemeral CI runner environment.
solution_steps:
1. Add a `pytest` autouse fixture in `conftest.py` to create schema tables on test setup and drop on teardown:
```python
import pytest
from backend.database import Base, engine

@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def setup_database():
    Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)
    yield
    Base.metadata.drop_all(bind=engine)
```
2. Commit `tests/conftest.py` and push.
verified_resolution: Added database schema creation fixture in conftest.py; all 18 CI unit tests passed.

title: Vite build fails: [vite:esbuild] Unexpected token '<' in JSX/TSX syntax error
description: When running npm run build, Vite throws a syntax error on JSX elements in file src/components/ChatCard.js.
error_log:
[vite:esbuild] Transform failed with 1 error:
src/components/ChatCard.js:14:6: ERROR: Unexpected "<"
  12 | return (
  13 |   <div className="card">
     |   ^
root_cause: Vite requires files containing JSX syntax to have the `.jsx` or `.tsx` extension instead of plain `.js`.
solution_steps:
1. Rename all React component files with JSX from `.js` to `.jsx`:
   `src/components/ChatCard.js` -> `src/components/ChatCard.jsx`
2. Update import statements if explicit file extensions were used.
3. Re-run `npm run build` or `npm run dev`.
verified_resolution: Renamed component files to .jsx; build succeeded in 850ms.

title: Pydantic ValidationError: 1 validation error for ChatRequest input_value
description: POST /api/chat returns HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity with error 'Field required'.
root_cause: The frontend was sending JSON payload with key `message` while the FastAPI Pydantic model expected key `query`.
solution_steps:
1. Align the frontend payload to match the Pydantic schema:
   `body: JSON.stringify({ query: userMessage })`
2. Or update Pydantic model with an alias:
```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

class ChatRequest(BaseModel):
    query: str = Field(alias="message", default="")
```
verified_resolution: Updated frontend payload key to 'query'; API responses returned 200 OK.

title: JWT Token Expired: 401 Unauthorized on authenticated routes
description: Interns logged into dashboard get booted out after 5 minutes with 401 Unauthorized.
root_cause: The JWT `exp` expiration claim was set to 5 minutes instead of 24 hours in `ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES`.
solution_steps:
1. In `config.py` or `.env`, update token expiry:
   `ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES = 60 * 24  # 24 hours`
2. Implement a silent refresh token mechanism in frontend axios interceptor.
verified_resolution: Increased access token lifetime and added token refresh handler.

title: npm ERR! ERESOLVE unable to resolve dependency tree during npm install
description: Running npm install in the dashboard project fails with ERESOLVE peer dependency conflicts between React 18 and an older Lucide package.
error_log:
npm ERR! code ERESOLVE
npm ERR! ERESOLVE unable to resolve dependency tree
npm ERR! Found: react@18.3.1
npm ERR! Could not resolve dependency: peer react@"^16.8.0 || ^17.0.0"
root_cause: NPM 7+ enforces strict peer dependency checking which halts installation on minor semver mismatches.
solution_steps:
1. Run install with legacy peer dependencies flag:
   `npm install --legacy-peer-deps`
2. Or update outdated packages to their React 18 compatible releases:
   `npm update lucide-react`
3. Delete `node_modules` and `package-lock.json` before re-running install.
verified_resolution: Ran npm install --legacy-peer-deps and updated lucide-react; installed cleanly.

title: React Maximum update depth exceeded: infinite loop inside useEffect
description: The analytics dashboard freezes the browser tab and console logs 'Maximum update depth exceeded'.
error_log: Uncaught Error: Maximum update depth exceeded. This can happen when a component repeatedly calls setState inside componentWillUpdate or componentDidUpdate.
root_cause: A `setState` call was made inside `useEffect` while including the updated state object itself inside the `useEffect` dependency array, creating an infinite render loop.
verified_resolution: Fixed dependency array in AnalyticsDashboard.jsx; infinite loop resolved.

title: Git LFS Error: GH008 Your push refers to a repository containing files larger than 100 MB
description: GitHub rejected my push because I accidentally committed a 140MB raw dataset `dataset.parquet` in my commit history.
error_log:
remote: error: GH008: Your push would contain a file larger than 100.00 MB.
remote: error: File data/raw_embeddings.bin is 142.50 MB; this exceeds GitHub's file size limit of 100.00 MB
root_cause: Large binary files (>100MB) cannot be pushed to standard GitHub repositories without Git LFS or purging from git history.
solution_steps:
1. Remove the large file from recent commit:
   `git rm --cached data/raw_embeddings.bin`
2. Add `*.bin` and `*.parquet` to `.gitignore`.
3. Amend previous commit:
   `git commit --amend -CHEAD`
4. If the file exists in older commits, run `git filter-branch` or `bfg --strip-blobs-bigger-than 50M`.
5. Re-push your branch.
verified_resolution: Unstaged large binary, updated .gitignore, amended commit, and push succeeded.
